  TUESDAY, AUGUST 19, 2025
  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 5:30 PM

Mary Zendejas, 1st District  Megan Kerr, 5th District
Cindy Allen, 2nd District  Dr. Suely Saro, 6th District
Kristina Duggan, 3rd District  Roberto Uranga, Vice Mayor, 7th District
Daryl Supernaw, 4th District  Tunua Thrash-Ntuk, 8th District
  Dr. Joni Ricks-Oddie, 9th District
Thomas B. Modica, City Manager
Monique De La Garza, City Clerk  Rex Richardson, Mayor  Dawn McIntosh, City Attorney

  REVISED

  SPECIAL MEETING

 MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC HAVE THE OPTION TO SUBMIT ONLINE PUBLIC COMMENTS AND
  EMAIL COMMENTS TO CITYCLERK@LONGBEACH.GOV

  PLEASE VIEW THE MEETING FROM YOUR COMPUTER, TABLET, OR SMARTPHONE
  VIA: HTTPS://LONGBEACH.PRIMEGOV.COM/PUBLIC/PORTAL?FROMIFRAME=TRUE

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

 NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
 The consent calendar shall be heard immediately after the pledge of allegiance, and prior to 6:30
 PM. All matters listed under the Consent Calendar are to be considered routine by the City Council
 and will all be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion of said items unless the
 Mayor, City Councilmembers or the City Manager request specific items be discussed and/or
 removed from the Consent Calendar for separate action.

 CONSENT CALENDAR (1 – 14)

 1.  25-56144  Recommendation to increase appropriations in the General Fund Group in the City
  Manager Department by $3,000, offset by the Eighth Council District One-Time
  District Priority Funds, transferred from the Citywide Activities Department, to
  provide contributions of:
  1. $3,000 to Care Closet LBC; and

  Decrease appropriations in the General Fund Group in the Citywide Activities
  Department by $3,000, to offset a transfer to the City Manager Department.

  Office or Department:  Tunua Thrash-Ntuk, Councilwoman, Eighth District

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

 2.  25-56146  Recommendation to correct the organization’s name receiving payment of $100,

  Page 1 of 11

  TUESDAY, AUGUST 19, 2025
  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 5:30 PM

  as authorized in the April 22, 2025 approved action, from The Long Beach Area
  Peace Network to Veterans for Peace.

  Office or Department:  Suely Saro, Councilwoman, Sixth District

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

3.  25-56148  Recommendation to increase appropriations in the General Fund Group in the City
  Manager Department by $200, offset by the Sixth Council District One-time District
  Priority Funds transferred from the Citywide Activities Department to provide a
  contribution to a New Way of Life Reentry Project to support their LaRonda Burton
  Memorial Recovery Awards on August 6, 2025; and

  Decrease appropriations in the General Fund Group in the Citywide Activities
  Department by $200, to offset a transfer to the City Manager Department.

  Office or Department:  Suely Saro, Councilwoman, Sixth District

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

4.  25-56112  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the City Council meeting of Tuesday,
  August 5, 2025.

  Office or Department:  City Clerk

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

5.  25-56113  Recommendation to refer to City Attorney damage claims received
  between August 4, 2025 and August 11, 2025.

  Office or Department:  City Clerk

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

6.  25-56114  Recommendation to approve the destruction of records for the Office of the City
  Clerk; and adopt resolution.

  Office or Department:  City Clerk

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

7.  25-56115  Recommendation to approve the destruction of records for the City Manager
  Department; and adopt resolution.

  Office or Department:  City Clerk

10. 25-56097  Recommendation to authorize City Manager, or designee, to execute a contract
  and all necessary documents, including any necessary subsequent amendments,
  with the County of Los Angeles, to receive and expend Department of Homeland
  Security grant funding for the 2024 Emergency Management Performance Grant
  (EMPG), in an amount not to exceed $65,120, for the period of July 1, 2024,
  through June 30, 2026; and

  Increase appropriations in the General Grants Fund Group in the Disaster
  Preparedness and Emergency Communications Department by $65,120, offset by
  grant reimbursement revenue. (Citywide)

  Office or Department:  Disaster Preparedness and Emergency
  Communications

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

11. 25-56098  Recommendation to authorize City Manager, or designee, to execute a Letter of
  Agreement, and all necessary documents including any subsequent amendments,
  with Interval House, from Long Beach, CA, to establish the continuation of
  coordinated assistance for victims of domestic violence, for a five-year period, at
  the discretion of the City Manager. (Citywide)

  Office or Department:  Police Department

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

12. 25-56099  Recommendation to authorize City Manager, or designee, to execute an
  Operational Agreement, and all necessary documents including any subsequent

  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD

  establish the continuation of coordinated assistance for victims of domestic
  violence and their families, for a five-year period, at the discretion of the City
  Manager. (Citywide)

  Office or Department:  Police Department

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

13. 25-56101  Recommendation to authorize City Manager, or designee, to allocate Public,
  Education, and Government (PEG) fee revenue equally among the three
  categories of cable access providers, each receiving one-third of the total
  available; and

  Increase appropriations in the General Services Fund Group in the Technology
  and Innovation Department by $593,394, offset by PEG fee revenue. (Citywide)

  Office or Department:  Technology and Innovation

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

14. 25-56102  Recommendation to authorize City Manager, or designee, to execute all
  documents necessary to amend Contract No. 36654 with Homeboy Recycling a
  California Social Purpose Corporation, dba Homeboy Electronics Recycling, of Los
  Angeles, CA, for providing technology waste services, to increase the contract
  amount to $50,000, annually with a 20 percent contingency in the amount of
  $10,000, for a revised annual contract amount not to exceed $60,000. (Citywide)

  Office or Department:  Technology and Innovation

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

  of the Proposed Fiscal Year 2026 Budget for the departments of Community
  Development and Health and Human Services and a presentation overview of
  Tidelands. (Citywide)

PUBLIC COMMENT: OBTAIN SPEAKER CARD FROM THE CITY CLERK
Opportunity to address the City Council (on non-agenda items) is given to the first 10 persons who
submit Speaker Cards to the City Clerk beginning at 15 minutes prior to the commencement of the
meeting. Each speaker is allowed three minutes to make their comments.

REGULAR AGENDA

16. 25-56137  Recommendation to request that the City Council approve the application of La
  Paz, Mexico as the City's newest Sister City, and authorize the Mayor of Long
  Beach to take necessary actions and execute any and all documents to
  accomplish the establishment of such a relationship.

  Office or Department:  Rex Richardson, Mayor

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

17. 25-56136  Recommendation to request City Manager to direct the proper departments to
  implement a Traffic Fatality Victim Memorial Sign Program similar to the one
  implemented on California Department of Transportation (CalTrans) right-of-ways
  in homage of traffic fatality victims. Further, this recommendation requests the
  program be codified into the Long Beach Municipal Code therefore, a draft
  ordinance for City Council review is requested from the Long Beach City Attorney’s
  office. The language in Assembly Bill 965, Statutes of 2001 is being provided and
  recommended for codification draft purposes.

  Office or Department:  Daryl Supernaw, Councilman, Fourth District

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

18. 25-56147  Recommendation to direct City Manager to work with the Government Affairs
  Office to revise the City’s Legislative Agenda to support policies, legislation, and
  funding that help facilitate the City’s responsible and strategic phase-out of local oil
  extraction operations including, but not limited to, measures that:
  • Modernize the State’s “surplus” finding and the associated revenue-sharing
  formula governing Long Beach’s tidelands oil and gas revenue;
  • Redirect interest revenues generated from the state’s oil abandonment
  liability savings or reinvest state oil revenues through direct appropriations
  back into Long Beach; and

  Direct City Manager to work with the Government Affairs Office to develop and

  Page 5 of 11
   CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
  TUESDAY, AUGUST 19, 2025
  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 5:30 PM

  present additional recommendations to the Intergovernmental Affairs Committee
  for discussion related to the responsible transition away from oil production and the
  protection of public trust resources. This discussion should include potential
  changes to the Legislative Agenda that would support strategies to mitigate budget
  impacts to core city services, limit employment losses and support the transition of
  displaced workers, and plan for future decommissioning and site remediation
  efforts.

  Office or Department:  Kristina Duggan, Councilmember, Third District; Cindy
  Allen, Councilwoman, Second District; Joni Ricks-
  Oddie, Councilmember, Ninth District

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

19. 25-56103  Recommendation to adopt Specifications No. RFP ED-25-602 and award a
  contract to Brown United, Inc., of Monrovia, CA, for the fabrication, transportation,
  and installation of the stage for the Long Beach Amphitheater, in a total amount of
  $1,600,000, authorize a five percent contingency in the amount of $80,000, for a
  total contract amount of $1,680,000, for a period of one year, at the discretion of
  the City Manager, or designee, to execute all documents necessary to enter into
  the contract, including any necessary subsequent amendments. (District 1)

  Office or Department:  Economic Development

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

20. 25-56104  Recommendation to adopt resolution authorizing City Manager, or designee, to
  execute a contract, and any necessary documents including any necessary
  subsequent amendments, with The Alpha & Omega Group Security Services, Inc.,
  of Inglewood, CA, for providing security guard services, on the same terms and
  conditions afforded to the County of Orange, CA, in an annual amount of
  $3,900,000, authorize a 20 percent contingency in the amount of $780,000, for a
  total annual contract amount not to exceed $4,680,000, until the County of Orange,
  CA contract expires on March 31, 2030, with the option to renew for as long as the
  County of Orange, CA contract is in effect, at the discretion of the City Manager.
  (Citywide)

  Office or Department:  Financial Management

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

21. 25-56105  Recommendation to adopt Specifications No. RFP CE-25-603 and award contracts
  to Fujitec America, Inc., of Santa Fe Springs, CA, and Specialized Elevator
  Services, LLC, of Santa Fe Springs, CA, for providing elevator installation,
  maintenance, repair, and related services, in an annual aggregate amount not to

  Page 6 of 11

  $220,000, for a total annual aggregate contract amount not to exceed $1,320,000,
  for a period of two years, with the option to renew for three additional one-year
  periods, at the discretion of the City Manager; and, authorize City Manager, or
  designee, to execute all documents necessary to enter into the contracts, including
  any necessary subsequent amendments. (Citywide)

  Office or Department:  Financial Management

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

22. 25-56106  Recommendation to receive and file a report on the requirements of Assembly Bill
  2561, which mandates local public agencies to present on the status of vacant
  positions, recruitment, and retention efforts prior to adoption of the City’s annual
  budget; and direct staff to comply with the provisions of the law. (Citywide)

  Office or Department:  Human Resources

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

23. 25-56107  Recommendation to authorize City Manager, or designee, to execute all
  documents necessary to amend Contract No. 34740 with Utility Solutions Partners,
  LLC, of Washington, DC, for managed services for providing maintenance and
  integration support related to the City of Long Beach’s utilities technology support
  and consultation services, in an annual contract amount of $2,529,916, plus a 5
  percent contingency in the amount of $126,496, for a revised annual contract
  amount of $2,656,412, and extend the term of the contract to September 30, 2026
  at the discretion of the City Manager. (Citywide)

  Office or Department:  Technology and Innovation

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

ORDINANCE

24. 25-56145  Recommendation to declare ordinance to approve, confirm, and ratify Ordinance
  No. HD-25-2490 of the Board of Harbor Commissioners of the City of Long Beach,
  which authorizes the Chief Executive Officer of the Long Beach Harbor
  Department to execute a Land Exchange Agreement between the City of Long
  Beach and the Los Angeles County Flood Control District, for the Pier B On-Dock
  Rail Support Facility Program, read the first time and laid over to the next regular
  meeting of the City Council for final reading. (District 7)

  Office or Department:  Harbor

   CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 5:30 PM

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

25. 25-56177  Recommendation to adopt ordinance approving a Zoning Code Amendment
  (ZCA24-002) to Section 21.39.030 of the Zoning Regulations in the Long Beach
  Municipal Code (LBMC), and adopt the proposed findings related thereto, to allow
  the Commercial Storage (CS) Zoning District to utilize height overlays pursuant to
  Chapter 21.39 of the Zoning Regulations, read and adopted as read; and

  25-56178  Adopt ordinance approving a Zoning Map Change (ZCHG24-004) request, and
  adopt the proposed findings related thereto, to amend the zoning designation from
  Light Industrial (IL) to CS, which also includes a high-rise overlay designation of
  fifty feet/5 stories (HR-50/5) in height, read and adopted as read.

  Office or Department:  Community Development

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

26. 25-56179  Recommendation to declare ordinance amending Sections 18.40.820, 18.40.830,
  18.41.300, and 18.41.310 of the Long Beach Municipal Code relating to enhanced
  drowning prevention measures for private swimming pools, read and adopted as
  read;

  25-56180  Declare ordinance amending Sections 18.40.275, 18.41.280 and 18.41.290 of the
  Long Beach Municipal Code relating to design requirements considering future
  sea-level for buildings in coastal flood hazard areas, read and adopted as read;
  and

  25-56181  Declare ordinance amending Section 18.79.020 of the Long Beach Municipal Code
  relating to clarifying requirements for subgrade electrical work in areas with
  potential methane gas, read and adopted as read. (Citywide)

  Office or Department:  Community Development

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.
